issues.description: getIamPolicy errors are swallowed and images silently reported as not publicly shared (false-negative PASS).
issues.detail: In _get_images the except block logs and leaves publicly_shared=False, so permission-denied or transient API errors become clean PASSes in a security tool. 'Unknown' and 'private' are different facts and must not collapse. Skip the image, surface UNKNOWN, or carry a tri-state on the model.

issues.description: Naming inconsistency between CHANGELOG/PR description and the on-disk check id.
issues.detail: Files and code use compute_image_not_publicly_shared, but the PR description and other references say compute_image_publicly_shared. Two identities for one thing will diverge across grep, dashboards, and suppressions. Pick one convention and apply it everywhere including docstrings and changelog.

issues.description: Per-image getIamPolicy calls are serial N+1, unlike the rest of the service which uses __threading_call__.
issues.detail: _get_images iterates images and issues one getIamPolicy per image on the calling thread, while sibling compute resources parallelize via __threading_call__. For projects with many custom images total time is N * RTT. Reuse the existing threading helper or batch the calls.

issues.description: Image model discards IAM bindings, collapsing data into a single boolean verdict.
issues.detail: The service walks bindings and keeps only publicly_shared, throwing away the policy data already fetched. This complects value with verdict and forces any future image-IAM check (overly permissive, external domain sharing) to redo the round trip. Store the relevant bindings or members on the model.

issues.description: Tests assert the boolean the test itself set; the real binding-parsing path in _get_images is never exercised.
issues.detail: Check tests construct Image(publicly_shared=True/False) directly, so they validate a trivial branch rather than extraction logic. Fixtures even configure a getIamPolicy error case but no test drives _get_images end-to-end through it. Add service-level tests that feed real bindings and exercise the IAM-error path.

issues.description: Exception logger dereferences error.__traceback__.tb_lineno, which can be None and raise a secondary AttributeError.
issues.detail: When an exception has no traceback attached (mocked or re-raised paths), tb_lineno access itself raises. It matches existing house style but is fragile, particularly with the test fixture's synthetic side_effect. Guard the attribute access or switch to logger.exception().

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a reasonable, well-scoped GCP check but NEEDS-WORK before landing. The dominant concern is that getIamPolicy errors silently produce PASS verdicts — wrong default for a security tool — compounded by an Image model that collapses bindings into a single boolean, hiding the data that justified the verdict. Naming is inconsistent across CHANGELOG, PR description, and filenames. Tests assert tautologies on hand-built Image objects rather than exercising the binding-parsing and IAM-error paths in _get_images. Secondary issues: serial N+1 getIamPolicy calls bypassing the existing __threading_call__ helper, and a fragile tb_lineno dereference in the exception logger.
